sections.content: How many people are "national government administrative occupations"?

189,835 people

were counted on the census as "national government administrative occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
National government administrative occupations undertake a variety of administrative and clerical duties in national government departments.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "national government administrative occupations" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "national government administrative occupations", 14.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "national government administrative occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "national government administrative occupations" included:

  • metal making and treating process operatives
  • welfare and housing associate professionals (other)
  • process operatives (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "national government administrative occupations" there were more women than men (57.6% compared with 42.4%).

This means "national government administrative occupations" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 42.4% and women made up 57.6% of "national government administrative occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "national government administrative occupations" included:

  • elementary administration occupations (other)
  • customer service managers
  • bar staff

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "national government administrative occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "national government administrative occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "national government administrative occupations", 15.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (79.6% compared with 20.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99.2%) than self-employed (0.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wiltshire, this is in the region of the South West.
